doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Sampling royalties and undocumented work
summary: He deposits sampling checks, regrets not documenting his work, and sees the music as a free gift.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Do you get checks in the mail from people who are sampling your music? Or do you get checks in the mail and you go what is this for?

Yeah. I get a lot of those. I don’t question it, I just put them in the bank. Thank you very much you know. Because if I tried to — you know one thing I haven’t done, I didn’t document everything that I have done. If like all that list you’ve got of me you know, if I had kept a list like that I could probably gather millions of dollars you know. But I didn’t document a lot of stuff. You know? And I don’t know what I did on what things — I just let a lot of stuff slip away. You know? But it’s a gift from God and so I can give it to whoever I want to have it. So if I played on your album or gave you some kind of inspiration or something then you’re welcome to it. Because it’s free for me and it’s free for you too.
